item.text:
Commercial deep-sea mining could add supply, but claiming it will end shortages is an unsupported guarantee. Here’s strong advocacy copy without that claim.

### (a) Three posts

1. We support commercial deep-sea mining because we need more sources of battery metals. We want investment that expands supply and tackles the bottlenecks holding battery production back.

2. We cannot build a battery-powered future without reliable mineral supplies. We back commercial deep-sea mining as part of a broader effort to strengthen supply chains, alongside processing and recycling.

3. We want action on battery-metal shortages. We support developing deep-sea mineral resources with enforceable environmental safeguards—and building the processing capacity needed to turn new supply into usable materials.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 106 words

We need a battery supply chain that can keep pace with our ambitions. That means confronting shortages with investment, infrastructure and additional sources of essential metals. We support commercial deep-sea mining as part of that effort, alongside recycling and expanded processing capacity. We want new mineral supplies matched by enforceable environmental safeguards, transparent oversight and clear accountability. We also recognise that extracting metals is only one step: refining, manufacturing and transportation must work together to deliver reliable supplies. Our position is straightforward: we should pursue deep-sea mineral development responsibly while addressing the bottlenecks that stand between available resources and the batteries our energy future will require.
